read_ts_us.description:
Read receipt timestamp (i64-µs) from the `message_reads` projection;
`null` = unread (bd-5icg).

tools.description: Acknowledge a message (private NIP-17 ack, idempotent).

message_id.description:
toron message id = the rumor's content-addressed hex EventId (NOT an
AM-style integer sequence). The arg is a string to match toron's own
id model — `fetch_inbox` returns `id` as hex; this accepts it verbatim.
(known-divergences §1: id-type differs by design per ADR-0003.)

tools.name: acknowledge_message

tools.description: Mark a message read (private NIP-17 read receipt, idempotent).

message_id.description: See [`AcknowledgeMessageArgs::message_id`] — hex event id, not an int.

tools.name: mark_message_read

reservation_ids.description:
Kind-30031 event id of each conflicting lease (bd-dsu1) — parallel to
`holders`, one id per holder. The operator lock board surfaces these
for diagnostics (force-release, request-release, replay).

soft_conflicts.description: ADR-0011 Spec 4: additive soft tier (in-TTL intents).

tools.description: Operator force-release of a stale reservation (staleness heuristic + revocation).

holder.description:
Optional holder name to disambiguate when multiple holders match the
path. Omit to revoke the (single) matching lease.

path.description:
Path (or glob) of the stale reservation to revoke. The daemon resolves
the active lease on this path itself (bd-cumj) — the caller does NOT
need the holder's event id.

project_key.description:
AM parity: `health_check` takes no required args. The field is kept
optional (default empty) so clients that mirror the project-scoped
convention still parse, but it is NOT required and NOT used — the
daemon reports process-global bus + archive health.
